evidence: Plaut. Aul. 215: tē cīvem sine malā omnī malitiā
Cic. Tusc. 4.34: nam malitia certī cujusdam vitiī nōmen est (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Cicero keeps it for one particular vice and says vitiōsitās for badness in general.

phrases.latin: Certē edepol equidem tē cīvem sine malā omnī malitiā semper sum arbitrātus et nunc arbitror.
phrases.english: Truly, I have always thought you a citizen without a trace of malice, and I think so still.
